brief: Explain a bond’s credit risk using a borrower unable to make a promised payment.

title.pt-BR: Uma promessa pode não ser cumprida

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Default Risk"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Una promesa puede incumplirse"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Uma promessa pode não ser cumprida"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Explain a bond’s credit risk using a borrower unable to make a promised payment.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: An interest promise is useful only if the borrower can actually make the payment.
instruction.misconception: A printed fixed payment eliminates borrower default risk.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: A bond promises payment, but the issuer runs out of money. The promise remains; the investor may receive less.
The borrower cannot meet its payment obligation.
Fixed terms do not ensure the issuer has money.
Missed payments directly concern the borrower’s reliability.
A good history does not eliminate future credit risk.
Failure to pay concerns the borrower’s obligation.
Lower receipts can prevent the promised debt payment.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.

en-US.line: An interest promise is useful only if the borrower can actually make the payment.

en-US.line: A bond promises payment, but the issuer runs out of money. The promise remains; the investor may receive less.

help: Ask whether the borrower can pay.
